findings.detail: Earlier question M3-S02-T2 already asks what tool use with a JSON schema justifies: it eliminates JSON syntax errors and nothing more. This question uses the same reasoning, only reframed as which old safeguard to remove. Option B nearly repeats a wrong option of M3-S02-T2 word for word (the schema itself converts inconsistent source formats into one standard form). Option A also repeats the semantic-error wrong option of M2-S60-T1 (a schema-valid output treated as proof that values are correct). So the wrong options mostly reuse earlier distractors, and the problem is not new.

blind_answer.reason: Tool use with a JSON schema eliminates JSON syntax errors such as missing brackets and unescaped quotes, so the repair script is no longer needed. It does not prevent semantic errors like a value placed in the wrong field (A). It does not normalize source formats, so the prompt normalization rules are still needed (B). Making every field required would push Claude to fabricate values (C).
